chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahb ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn Isa ibn Abdullah Al-Qummi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray the morning prayer with 'Amma Yatasaa'loon', 'Hal Ataka Hadith Al-Ghashiyah', 'La Uqsimu Biyawm Al-Qiyamah', and similar surahs. He would pray the noon prayer with 'Sabbih Isma', 'Ash-Shamsi Wa Duhaaha', 'Hal Ataka Hadith Al-Ghashiyah', and similar surahs. He would pray the sunset prayer with 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad', 'Idha Ja'a Nasr Allah Wal-Fath', and 'Idha Zulzilat'. He would pray the last part of the night prayer in a manner similar to what he prayed in the noon prayer, and the afternoon prayer in a manner similar to the sunset prayer.

key_terms.الشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا: The Sun and its brightness (Surah Ash-Shams)
key_terms.سَبِّحِ اسْمَ: Glorify the name of your Lord (Surah Al-A'la)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)
key_terms.هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ الْغَاشِيَةِ: Has there reached you the news of the Overwhelming (Surah Al-Ghashiyah)

ai.seo_question: What surahs did the Prophet Muhammad typically recite in each of the five daily prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) consistent practice of reciting specific surahs during the five daily prayers, reflecting a structured yet flexible approach to *qira'ah*. It underscores the scholarly emphasis on following the Prophet’s habitual recitations as a model for devotional consistency, while allowing for variations in length and content based on the time of day and congregational needs.
